# Plan: release cadence optimization

**Date:** 2026-09-28  
**Phase:** `agent-fabric-convergence::release-cadence-optimization`  
**Stage:** plan draft for isolated review and operator feedback; execute is not authorized by this document.  
**Backend:** OpenSpec is present. Root owns change scaffolding and canonical KBD commands.  
**Change count:** one process change, `afc-release-cadence-optimization`, with four bounded tasks.  
**Product-code scope:** none in this child. Approved execute work here **applies** authored roadmap/process and agent-team instruction changes; the parent implements the subsequent UAR/Boss shipping increments in their owning repositories.

The [assessment](assessment.md) and [analysis](analysis.md) show a real gap: C06/C07 have local UAR integration receipts, yet the latest initiative-accepted installed Boss release is 2.2.3 P1; C08 remains open with an observed E0382 compile failure. Current `pnpm build:mac:arm64` disables UAR, and canonical payload import requires both Windows x64 and Mac ARM64 records. This process child must make a **reviewable shipping contract and parent roadmap handoff**, not silently change product scripts or call a source checkpoint a release. The target of one local delivery per elapsed hour includes waits/build time and remains unproven; a cold compile can exceed it. Count aggregate agent effort separately and report an overrun honestly.

## One ordered OpenSpec change

### `afc-release-cadence-optimization` — make full-stack local deliveries measurable and releasable

- **Scope:** Process and authored roadmap/team sources: this child's delivery/operating contract and final receipt; initiative `docs/plans/agent-fabric-convergence/.kbd-orchestrator/phases/agent-fabric-convergence/plan.md`, `docs/plans/agent-fabric-convergence/work-packages.json`, `docs/plans/agent-fabric-convergence/dependencies.md` and relevant recommendation mappings; active BossFang `.agent-team/bossfang-stewards/team.json`, its generated `.codex/agents/*.toml` and `.claude/agents/*.md` role exports, and targeted authored repo instructions only where the test-first conflict actually persists. Scope must be widened through the supported child-scope mechanism before execute. Root-owned signed-receipt OpenSpec mirror reconciliation creates no new product completion. No edits to The Boss/UAR product code, current C08 source, generated KBD waypoints/tasks, or release workflows.
- **Depends on:** Assessment and analysis feedback; accepted C01 contract for status vocabulary. It does **not** depend on C08 completion. C08's compiler fix and real gate remain with its owner. C09 has its own C02/C03/C04/C06 prerequisites and may proceed independently under exact owner/checkpoint claims.
- **Recommended agent:** `bossfang-stewards` product-manager for the authored parent roadmap; agent-team owner for the active team manifest and native exports; release, UAR runtime and Boss UI owners for contract accuracy. Root KBD lead handles typed parent plan revision, canonical registration and isolated process-artifact review. No product verifier is dispatched before a complete shipping boundary.
- **Est. complexity:** M (one process/documentation session after approved inputs; no hour guarantee for later product delivery).
- **Complexity score:** High because applying the cross-repository roadmap and active team export while preserving canonical ownership is an architecture change, even though each authored edit is bounded.
- **Model class:** frontier for this change's plan and cross-repository contract execution; a focused writer may use medium only when the KBD task router records a separate medium-scored assignment under the active model policy.
- **Customer value:** High if the handoff results in a working packaged Boss sooner; this child by itself ships no customer capability.
- **Reuse:** `cand-001` existing electron-builder/Mac package path **adapt**; `cand-002` UAR sidecar packaging/local record **adapt**; `cand-003` frozen release jobs **adapt**; `cand-004` agent-team ownership **adapt**; `cand-005` KBD/OpenSpec/Karpathy **adopt**; `cand-006` incremental Compass **adapt**. Reject `cand-007` all-platform builds on each local hourly critical path and `cand-008` runtime-only sidecar override as packaged acceptance. No dependency upgrade, new scheduler, daemon or telemetry framework.

#### Task 1.1 — Freeze a truthful local-delivery and publication contract

**Owner/write surface:** Product-manager authors `delivery-contract.md` in this child. Release owner and Boss/UAR owners review it read-only. Task 1.2 applies its accepted rules to the authored parent roadmap in the same child execute.

**Required content:** Define a delivery as a complete user journey with UAR/core implementation, Boss UI, typed IPC/host adapter, i18n, persistence/settings, governance and two-workspace isolation where relevant. Finish all production wiring before one phase-end integration gate and the actual local `pnpm build:mac:arm64`; open/launch the newly packaged app with runtime sidecar overrides cleared and demonstrate the new UI action and packaged UAR source/version/effective port. Record both source commits, helper and app hashes, output path, runtime result and capability limits. DMG integrity, a sidecar-only query, or `THE_BOSS_UAR_SIDECAR_PATH` override alone does not qualify.

The **first subsequent parent shipping increment** owns the observed shell-recipe repair: today exact `pnpm build:mac:arm64` forces UAR off. Propose a source-frozen local-only checksummed arm64 sidecar overlay, paired to clean committed UAR and Boss revisions, so local Mac packaging does not wait for a Windows artifact. Preserve the existing canonical importer: CI/public preflight rejects any local overlay and still requires both immutable win32-x64 and darwin-arm64 records from the same UAR SHA. `extraResources` places the executable outside ASAR; the actual product packaging path must be proved at the later shipping gate. This child writes the task specification only; no script is fixed here.

After **every successful local delivery**, ask the operator: **“Publish this version for all macOS and Windows targets now, or wait until the next delivery?”** No answer is not publication approval. “All” means darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, win32-x64 and win32-arm64, never Linux. Current UAR-enabled release support is evidenced only for darwin-arm64 and win32-x64; the parent must implement native UAR payload/profile support for the other two before advertising all four. If publish-now is selected while a target is missing, record the target blocker and complete it rather than ship a non-UAR substitute. Freeze source/version/profile, publish each exact native artifact, serialize release metadata/site updates, retain prior working links, and record per-platform built/published/installed status. Publication work and waiting remain in elapsed delivery time even if the next independent code increment begins.

**Acceptance of 1.1:** A reviewer can follow the contract from clean source to local package to a binary that launches from its own resources, to the operator's platform decision and four distinct publication states. It clearly assigns shell/profile and missing-platform implementation to the next parent shipping change, not to this child.

#### Task 1.2 — Apply a lossless parent roadmap and dependency revision

**Owner/write surface:** Product-manager owns this child's `roadmap-handoff.md` **and the authored parent** `docs/plans/agent-fabric-convergence/.kbd-orchestrator/phases/agent-fabric-convergence/plan.md`, `docs/plans/agent-fabric-convergence/work-packages.json`, `docs/plans/agent-fabric-convergence/dependencies.md`, and any directly corresponding authored `recommendations.json` rows. UAR, Boss, C08, Gate, Fabric and release owners validate only their owned contract rows. Root records the typed KBD parent plan revision with `prometheus kbd --path <initiative> revise --reason <reason> --exact-next-work <work>`; this revises the run plan without activating the parent or manually editing projections. Widen the advisory child write scope before execute.

**Required content:** Apply the approved local-delivery contract to the parent execution sequence while preserving all C01–C18 titles, original IDs, recommendation IDs, acceptance requirements and historical evidence. Make D1 a **dispatchable first product delivery** in the revised parent plan: repair exact `pnpm build:mac:arm64` to package clean-source UAR through a local-only checksummed arm64 input with CI refusal, and expose already accepted C06/C07 instance activation and observer recovery through existing Boss UI, typed IPC, settings/persistence and all locales. D1 ends with one complete real-path integration/packaged-launch gate; it is not executed in this child. Assign exact repository owners and required native payload revisions as dispatch preconditions. Preserve C08's own compiler/gate work and separate source/compiled/integrated/installed/published states; C09 can start under its C02/C03/C04/C06 dependencies without waiting for C08. A catalog view is not a standalone default delivery; include catalog management with an operational team journey unless the operator expressly accepts management alone. The first effectful team delivery contains all C09.1–C09.3 plus Boss team/member/task UI and restrictive C02 governance. Do not split it into mock-only phases just to create a test boundary. It may overrun one hour; do not delay C09 core for cosmetic UI filler.

The parent revision may move **bounded C14.1 visibility/operation scope** to D1 only if the revised dependency wording makes that early contract exact; C14 as a whole remains open. Similarly, a later direct C10 workflow before C08 needs its own explicit approved dependency change and cannot close C10's required BossFang/channel path. Retain C11–C18, all external checkpoints and rollback limits. This is an applied authored roadmap, not a competing plan in a handoff file; root records the revision using supported KBD commands after the authored edit.

Bounded ledger reconciliation belongs here because current `openspec list` reportedly shows C06 **0/3** against its signed canonical accepted receipt and C08 **0/3** against canonical **1/3**. Root must inspect the exact canonical task IDs and signed receipts before changing any mirror; parent OpenSpec uses ordinals `1.1–1.3` with textual `Initiative task: C09.1`-style mappings, so map by the actual text and receipt rather than passing a guessed C ID as the OpenSpec ordinal. If IDs match, use only `node scripts/kbd-apply.mjs mark-done` for already-complete parent OpenSpec tasks, then record mirror result and source revision. That command updates the backend checkbox without a canonical transition. **Never** use `begin-task` or `end-task` on the parent while this child is active: those commands resolve the active child phase. Do not infer a completion, edit generated `tasks.md`/waypoints, or expand into a repository-wide audit. A mirror mismatch stays open with a cited reason.

C08's observed compiler failure and source-only/service-probe evidence remain open with the C08 owner. C08 does **not** block independent C09 because C09 depends on C02/C03/C04/C06, not C08. C10 direct Boss feedback and the BossFang/channel path need explicit separately reviewable contracts if the parent considers advancing direct workflow; the parent C10 acceptance and C08 dependency cannot be silently marked complete. All effectful routes retain current authority, two-workspace isolation, exact effect receipts and uncertain-outcome behavior. C11/C12 tracks, C13 profiles, C15 skills, C16 specialists, C17 representation and C18 federation/release evidence stay mapped and owned.

**Acceptance of 1.2:** Authored parent plan, work packages, dependencies and recommendation mappings agree on D1, its ownership, C08/C09 independence, early bounded C14 credit and all retained C01–C18 requirements. Original dependencies and any approved changed edges are both visible; historical completions are unchanged. Existing signed C06/C08 parent receipts and OpenSpec mirrors agree where evidence warrants; any unmatched row is recorded open. No parent task is newly completed by this child revision.

#### Task 1.3 — Repair active team instructions and attach bounded learning

**Owner/write surface:** Agent-team owner edits the active BossFang `.agent-team/bossfang-stewards/team.json` source and regenerates only the affected `.codex/agents/*.toml` and `.claude/agents/*.md` exports through its existing team lifecycle. Product-manager authors the concise `operating-contract.md` and initiative dispatch instructions. Update authored repository instruction source only if an exact conflicting line still routes this initiative to early checks; preserve unrelated guidance and generate derived instructions through the owning mechanism. Record each owning source revision in the implementation receipt. Mini/full agent-team creator/manage/handoff/models skills are already compliant with phase-boundary verification: **do not edit them just because they are available**. Their clean source anchors are mini `prometheus-skills-mini-hma-integration` at `31fb2ce` (`skills/agent-team-{creator,manage,handoff,models}`) and full `hma-full-pack` at `814d476` (`skills/process/agent-team-*`); do not commandeer those active HMA worktrees. If an actual adapter conflict is discovered during execute, use a suitable free/reused managed worktree from its owning committed baseline and a narrowly approved scope, otherwise record compatibility unchanged.

**Required content:** In the active team manifest and affected native exports, replace observed `test-first` directions in `surrealdb-schema-engineer` and `bossfang-feature-steward`, and any targeted cargo-check/test ladder conflict for this initiative, with the operator's **whole independently shipping phase first, then one integration/build gate** rule. The manifest has `schemaVersion`, `id`, `outcome`, `scope`, `harness`, `modelPolicy` and `roles`; preserve those fields, existing Claude routing and model selections. Generate Codex exports additively without silently switching the active harness/team, and preserve upstream-merge requirements and unrelated roles. State the rule's precedence in the actual routed instruction surface. Name four nonoverlapping lanes: UAR Rust runtime/storage; Boss UI/IPC/i18n/preferences; native payload/release; read-only delivery observer/ledger. Reserve one heavy local Rust/Electron packaging writer; other lanes may edit their own unfrozen surfaces or documents, but no second expensive compile/Compass scan overlaps the build on this host. At source freeze, stop edits to that snapshot until gate/package result. Add the bounded delivery-optimization observer through the **existing team definition/lifecycle/export**, scoped to observing logs and advising; it cannot add tests, revise scope, dispatch production work, mark acceptance or override a feedback stop. Use explicit KBD/Karpathy boundary recording; mini's automatic Karpathy hooks are not wired. No new runtime, daemon or telemetry framework.

For each delivery record **elapsed critical path** from start through functioning local build, with waits/build included; also record aggregate active agent minutes when observable, blocked time, build/gate time, first usable-app time, rework and any subsequent platform publication/installed result. Unknown durations remain null, not zero. The single C01.1 Karpathy event with `elapsedHours: 0.0` proves a logged boundary, not productivity. Bounded Compass refresh is a queued incremental update for changed active worktrees at roughly hourly active-work boundaries; serialize with the heavy writer, record deferral and graph revision, then query affected symbols. The 134.98-second, ~0.88 GB cold partial graph is a measured baseline, not a recurring-cost estimate or authority for negative lookups. Do not install an automation or rerun a full clean-root index just to satisfy a clock.

**Acceptance of 1.3:** Active manifest and affected Codex/Claude exports agree on phase-boundary testing, four owner lanes, resource admission and observer limits while retaining unrelated roles/models. The implementation receipt names exact changed source revision(s), regenerated outputs and any repo-rule line changed; full/mini skill sources are either recorded compatible and untouched or changed only for an observed conflict in their own approved worktree. Clock definitions and explicit boundary invocation are sufficient for D1 dispatch without inventing agent-time data.

#### Task 1.4 — Run one process-artifact consistency gate and hand off

**Owner/write surface:** KBD lead owns the single completed-child artifact gate and `handoff-out.md`; product-manager and agent-team owner resolve findings in their assigned authored files. Independent reviewer examines process completeness once, **after** tasks 1.1–1.3 are complete. Root runs supported OpenSpec/KBD registration, typed plan revision and stage transitions; this writer does not edit generated projections.

**Gate:** Compare `delivery-contract.md`, `roadmap-handoff.md`, `operating-contract.md`, the **revised authored parent** plan/work packages/dependencies/recommendation rows, active team manifest and regenerated role exports, and the assessment/analysis. Confirm every target, dependency, owner, status boundary, clock, feedback stop and candidate is consistent and that D1 can be dispatched from the parent without another planning cycle. Resolve critical contradictions once; record bounded findings and limitations. This is a **process artifact consistency gate**, not a product build, service gate, native installer test or claim that the hourly target was met.

**Exit:** Hand the **applied authored parent roadmap** and active team policy, exact D1 shipping task (repair the UAR-enabled local Mac build recipe/payload provenance while delivering a real Boss journey), reserved owners, and C08/C09 parallel boundary to the parent. Stop after execute for operator feedback; do not enter reflect or restore the parent waypoint until reflect is authorized and completed.

## Execution order, scope and feedback stops

1. Root registers this **one** OpenSpec change and tasks 1.1–1.4 through supported commands after plan review. No new parent C tasks are registered here.
2. Process execute: 1.1 delivery/release contract; 1.2 **apply** authored parent roadmap/requirement revisions plus bounded signed-receipt OpenSpec mirror reconciliation by root; 1.3 **apply** active team-role/export and any observed repo-rule repair, with concise ownership/metrics/Compass dispatch contract. This child performs no product edits or tests and authorizes no new product dispatch before its handoff.
3. After 1.1–1.3 are complete, 1.4 performs **one** process artifact consistency gate and writes a truthful handoff. Fix only findings from that gate and repeat the failed check if necessary. It does not trigger C08/C09 product tests or a standalone build.
4. Stop for operator feedback after execute. Reflect, OpenSpec archive and parent waypoint restoration require their own later authorized stage; no completion claim at four checked boxes alone. After authorized reflect restores the **C08 return point**, the parent uses the **already revised** plan to dispatch D1 and dependency-ready C09 under exact owners; no second planning round or forced fresh assess/analyze cycle is needed for that approved scope. C08 source/gate work remains owned and open.

The later parent shipping increment must itself complete production code before its single product integration/build gate. Each successful local UAR-enabled Mac app then prompts the all-four-macOS/Windows publication choice. If no functioning app exists at the hour boundary, report source/compiled/integrated/installed/published status and overrun, keep implementing, and **do not** call it an hourly delivery. No Linux target is added. The parent remains accountable for the C08 compiler/gate and may advance dependency-ready C09 independently under exact ownership.

## Review questions before execute

- Does the child-to-parent handoff keep all product fixes outside this process scope while making the *first* shipping task specific enough to dispatch?
- Does the local-only sidecar overlay remain provably separate from CI/release payloads, with clean committed provenance and no runtime path override accepted as package proof?
- Can a reviewer trace every C01–C18 requirement to its original owner and see that advancing a portion of C14 or C10 does not erase the remainder?
- Are the hour clock, publication choice, target gaps and one heavy build writer stated without promising an unmeasured one-hour compile?
- Does the team/rule handoff resolve the observed test-first conflict without starting a new per-edit test loop?

Unresolved until parent product execution: measured cold/native build duration; implementation and acceptance of the local-only overlay; Mac Intel/Windows ARM64 UAR payload support; whether catalog management has independent customer value; external-account acceptance for later C10; C08 channel-source gate. The authored dependency amendments are made during this child execute, not deferred for another planning round. None of the remaining product work is silently waived.

## Dispatch details carried into the parent revision

**D1 — a fresh local Boss with durable-agent controls:** Reconcile current Boss main `1fe9acff` and the older convergence Boss worktree `48070346` in an owned checkout; preserve unrelated changes, record the chosen source rather than silently building the older checkout. Release owner owns `package.json`, `scripts/integration-binaries.js`, `scripts/download-binaries.js`, `scripts/uar-payload-integrity.cjs` and a small local payload resolver only if required. Reuse UAR `scripts/package-boss-sidecar.mjs` from the selected clean UAR commit. Boss UI owner owns existing `UarAdministrationWorkspace.tsx`, trusted `UarAdministrationAdapter.ts`, shared IPC, preference definitions and locale keys for instance lifecycle/observer status; confirm exact source paths and reserve them before dispatch. These owners share a frozen payload/IPC contract, never the same output directory. A cached sidecar can be reused only when its recorded source matches the selected runtime source. No stale payload may stand in for changed UAR code.

**D2 — operational bounded team:** Full C09 domain, durable tasks/mailbox/claims, budgets and restrictive delegation, plus reachable Boss team controls, membership/task state and restart/cancel behavior. Catalog administration comes with this functioning journey. Core work may start alongside independent D1 source work when file claims do not overlap; it cannot mutate D1's frozen runtime snapshot. One heavy local builder; D1 publication does not wait for D2.

**D3 — feedback to approved issue:** Preserve C10's C08 dependency by default; only an explicitly scoped direct-path amendment approved by the operator can change it. No unseen dependency removal under this child approval. Keep channel/BossFang and uncertain external-effect requirements open until evidenced.

**Platform publication track:** Native release owner must supply the missing Mac Intel and Windows ARM64 UAR build/profile support, in addition to Windows x64/Apple Silicon. This is a required tracked item, not a reason to stall local Mac delivery. Every publish-now choice binds to a frozen delivery version/commit set. Retain each previous platform link until replacement succeeds; the single metadata publisher refuses to regress a newer version when an older job finishes. Report each platform honestly. GitHub Releases and the landing site remain the publication targets, never IPFS.

**Concurrency and adaptation:** After1.1, tasks1.2 and1.3 may run in parallel with distinct writers; root alone applies canonical revisions/mirrors. Product phases use up to the active harness slot limit (currently four including lead); do not spawn four workers plus a lead. The observer replaces an idle slot for a bounded checkpoint, not an always-running extra agent. At the first halfway checkpoint (~30elapsed minutes), forecast completion using recorded build durations; do not invent estimates from commits. If the budget cannot fit, choose a smaller already approved independent next increment and disclose current overrun. Never discard an in-progress safety requirement or trigger a partial gate. A cold build's missing timing remains unknown.

**One lightweight receipt:** Store per-delivery ID/C requirement mapping, owner/file claims, start/freeze/local-ready times, Boss/UAR/skill revisions, build+gate outcome, versioned artifact path and SHA256, effective sidecar port, user-visible journey, graph revision/coverage and publication decision/status. Link it from existing Karpathy boundary events; no second task ledger or custom daemon. Summed agent minutes may be unavailable and MUST be labeled so. An hourly graph deadline missed due to the heavy writer is logged and serviced immediately after release of that writer.

# Goals — agent-fabric-convergence > release-cadence-optimization

- Target a useful independently releasable increment per hour of active agent runtime with The Boss UI delivered alongside core capability.
- Reserve production tests and builds for completed independently shipping phase boundaries.
- Use resource-aware concurrent agent ownership across Rust, TypeScript UI, documentation and release work.
- Use Karpathy evidence to propose a delivery optimization role and measure bottlenecks without inventing timings.
- Refresh and use Compass code graphs hourly during active work with bounded resource use.
- Follow assess analyze plan execute reflect and wait for operator feedback after each stage; preserve parent work and return point.

## Operator clarification after Assess — 2026-09-28

Every hourly delivery must end with a functioning local Apple Silicon application produced by the exact command `pnpm build:mac:arm64`, with the completed functionality reachable in The Boss. For UAR increments, the application must package and run the corresponding UAR source. A successful compile or DMG integrity check alone does not establish functioning.

After EACH local delivery ask whether to update all macOS and Windows targets now or wait until the next delivery. Linux is excluded. No answer is not publication approval. Track darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, win32-x64 and win32-arm64 separately; current UAR support gaps cannot be hidden by publishing a non-UAR build.

Cadence planning will count elapsed delivery time, including build and waits, with aggregate agent effort separately recorded when observable. This is a planning interpretation, not a measured hourly guarantee. Preserve stage feedback stops: Analyze was authorized at that checkpoint. The operator subsequently approved Plan with “Yes, plan.”; Execute still awaits feedback.
